 SC upholds P83-M tax refund for San Miguel Brewery 
 November 15, 2026 | 9:16 pm 
 SANMIGUEL.COM.PH 
 THE Supreme Court (SC) has upheld a P83.02-million tax refund or tax credit for San Miguel Brewery, Inc., affirming a Court of Tax Appeals (CTA) ruling involving excess excise taxes collected on San Mig Light products in 2013. 
 In a decision promulgated on Oct. 28, the High Court’s First Division denied the petition for review filed by the Commissioner of Internal Revenue, sustaining the tax court’s ruling that the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) imposed excise tax rates exceeding those authorized by law. 
 The decision, penned by Associate Justice Ramon Paul L. Hernando, upheld San Miguel Brewery’s entitlement to a refund or tax credit certificate amounting to P83,018,504.21.
 The case stemmed from the implementation of Republic Act No. 10351, or the Sin Tax Reform Law, which introduced revised excise tax rates on fermented liquors beginning Jan. 1, 2013. 
 Under the law, fermented liquors with a net retail price of P50.60 or less per liter were taxed at P15 in 2013, while those priced above that threshold were taxed at P20 per liter.
 However, BIR Revenue Memorandum Circular No. 90-2012 prescribed a uniform excise tax rate of P20.57 per liter for bottled and canned San Mig Light.
 San Miguel Brewery paid the prescribed taxes to allow the release of its products from its breweries before seeking a refund of the excess payments.
 The company argued that the BIR circular imposed excise taxes beyond the rates authorized under the amended National Internal Revenue Code.
 The Supreme Court upheld the tax court’s determination that the BIR could not impose excise tax rates exceeding those prescribed by Congress through an administrative issuance. — Erika Mae P. Sinaking
